newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Irish EU Presidency sees three possible deals.
newsitem.headline: Irish EU Presidency sees three possible deals.

text.p: Agreement is possible this month on veal crates, cereals penalties and protection of regional foods, according to the Irish EU Presdidency.
The presidency noted at a meeting of the Special Committee on Agriculture that the European Parliament had either given an opinion on these issues or would do so at its session next week.

In November, the parliament said veal crates should be banned in view of public concern about the suffering they caused calves. The Commission proposed on January 24 (COM 96 21) to ban all veal crates for rearing calves from 2008. New or renovated crates would be banned from 1998 and old crates phased out over 10 years. French, Italian, Dutch and Belgian farmers, the main users of veal crates, have protested that the proposal would ruin them.

The Commission has proposed, following German demands, modifying Regulation 1765/92 to allow penalties for exceeding annual planting base areas to be targeted at the regions responsible. Currently, member states whose farmers exceed base area limits face a one percent cut in aid for every one percent overplanting.

The Commission has proposed that a five-year transitional period for implementing new rules on the protection of feta cheese and other regional foodstuffs (Regulation 2081/92 should expire in July 2002. The new rules were due to have come into force on July 25, 1997.
EU officials said the Irish EU Presidency did not envisage any agreement on the following issues during its six-month term ending on December 31:

An opinion is still awaited from the European Parliament on a proposal from the Commission in July (COM(96)361) to fix a maximum guaranteed area for each member state that would be shared between traditional producers. On November 18, farm ministers demanded that an extra 650,000 hectares should be included in the area aid scheme. In 1996, farmers planted 3.2 million hectares of durum wheat.

An opinion is not expected this month from the European Parliament on a Commission proposal of October 3 (COM(96)460). At their last meeting on November 18, farm ministers said more work was needed. Several said the proposed start-up dates were unrealistic and they needed more time to set up a computerised system. On labelling, ministers were split on whether the scheme should be compulsory or voluntary. - Potatoes:

Although the Parliament has given its opinion, farm ministers were deeply split on November 18 over an Irish compromise on a 1992 proposal (COM(92)185) for a lightweight regime. The incoming Dutch Presidency is also unenthusiastic about the proposal.
